title: The Canal Dug by a Famine | Buckingham Canal, Chennai #shorts

lines.text: A canal in Chennai was dug by people who were starving.
lines.caps: a canal in *Chennai | dug by people | who were *starving.

lines.text: In eighteen seventy six the monsoon failed, and famine spread across the Madras Presidency.
Across India, millions died. Estimates run from about five million to over nine million.
lines.caps: across India | *millions died | about *five million | to over *nine.

lines.text: Relief came with a condition. To be fed, you had to work.
lines.caps: relief came with | a *condition | to be fed | you had to *work.

lines.text: In early eighteen seventy seven, the daily relief wage for a man was cut to one pound of grain, and one anna.
lines.caps: in early *1877 | the wage was cut | to *one pound | of grain.

lines.text: Women and children got less. Even the sanitary commissioner of Madras argued for at least one and a half pounds.
lines.caps: women and children | got *less | even the *sanitary commissioner | argued for *more.

lines.text: One of these relief works was a canal through the city of Madras.
lines.caps: one relief work | was a *canal | through *Madras.

lines.text: Workers dug a link about eight kilometres long, joining the Adyar river to the Cooum.
lines.caps: a link about | *8 kilometres | joining the *Adyar | to the *Cooum.

lines.text: It was ordered by the Governor, the Duke of Buckingham.
lines.caps: ordered by | the *Governor | the Duke of *Buckingham.

lines.text: And the canal took his name. The diggers left no names that we know of.
lines.caps: the canal took | *his name | the *diggers | left *no names.

lines.text: Joined to older stretches, the Buckingham Canal runs about seven hundred and ninety six kilometres along the coast.
lines.caps: joined to older stretches | it runs about | *796 km | along the *coast.

lines.text: Today, in Chennai, long stretches lie choked and neglected.
lines.caps: today in Chennai | long stretches | lie *choked.

lines.text: So the next time you cross it, remember who dug it.
lines.caps: next time you *cross it | remember | who *dug it.

sources.name: Buckingham Canal (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: the 8 km Adyar-Cooum link built in 1877-78 as famine relief work; named after the Governor, the Duke of Buckingham and Chandos, who ordered it; earlier stretches from 1806 (Cochrane's Canal); total length about 796 km along the Coromandel coast

sources.name: Great Famine of 1876-1878 (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: monsoon failure and drought from 1876; death toll estimates from about 5.5 million to 9.6 million across India (official figure about 5.2 million); the 'Temple wage' of 1 lb of grain plus one anna for a man on relief works from January 1877, less for women and children; Sanitary Commissioner W. R. Cornish arguing for at least 1.5 lb

sources.name: The Duke who gave us a canal (Sriram V, Madras Musings)
sources.supports: a food-for-work programme begun during the famine that involved digging the canal through Madras, named after the Governor

sources.name: Buckingham Canal: Undoing 150 years of damage (DT Next)
sources.supports: the canal's present neglected and polluted state in Chennai

illustration: All figures are faceless shadow silhouettes; no portraits of real people (including the Duke) are shown. Grain, coins, notices and maps are illustrations with no real document text. Maps are stylised, not to scale.
uncertain: Death toll estimates for the famine vary widely (official about 5.2 million; later estimates up to about 9.6 million across India). Madras-only figures are not given in the video.
Sources differ on when the name Buckingham Canal came into use (1878 in some, the 1880s in others); the video only says the canal took his name.
The 796 km length covers the whole canal from Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh; the famine-relief link in Chennai is only about 8 km of it.
That the diggers' names were not recorded is phrased 'that we know of'.
The 1 lb wage was the scale set in January 1877; Madras moved to a revised scale in March 1877.
